open_points.subject: A13 rule 5 vs resume semantics for dependants of `service_unreachable`
open_points.text: "`service_unreachable` and `outcome_unknown` are waits, not failures, and their dependants wait, until the owner's resolution makes the element count as succeeded or failed (A11 rule 3)."
open_points.question: For dependants blocked by `service_unreachable`, what event unblocks them: only owner resolution (as written), or a later successful resend via `resume`?
options: Dependants of `service_unreachable` unblock when a resumed attempt concludes (without owner resolution).
Dependants of `service_unreachable` remain blocked until an owner resolution step (mirroring `outcome_unknown`).
open_points.default_guess: Dependants unblock after resume-driven reattempt conclusion; owner resolution applies only to `outcome_unknown`.

open_points.subject: Send-time handling of duplicate `required_headers` in selected instance
open_points.text: A08 rule 6: "...fails one of rule 5's checks of the record itself — not those of the instance, which are A09 rule 6's own..."; A09 rule 1: "...a record naming one header twice so is a manifest mismatch"; A09 rule 6 pre-send checks do not explicitly list duplicate required-header names.
open_points.question: If the selected instance now has duplicate required-header names (case-insensitive), which check rejects it at send time and what exact failure detail is recorded?
options: Treat as A09 rule 6 second pre-send check (instance invalid) with an operation_failed detail for duplicate required headers.
Treat as A08 `binding_stale` despite being an instance-level issue.
Allow send and rely on HTTP layer/header merge behavior.
open_points.default_guess: Reject in A09 pre-send instance check as `operation_failed` with a specific duplicate-required-header detail.

open_points.subject: A18 runtime symlink/store-call failure effect on in-flight run/request
open_points.text: A18 rule 2: "...a link found later makes that store call fail with nothing written."
open_points.question: When this happens during run advancement (or any mutating request), what externally visible outcome is required: request refusal only, kernel stop, run marked failed, or retry behavior?
options: Fail only the current request with internal refusal; keep process running; run state unchanged except prior committed records.
Stop kernel process immediately to preserve store trust boundary.
Mark affected run `failed` with a synthetic trace record.
Retry store call after re-checking filesystem.
open_points.default_guess: Fail current request/store call atomically and keep kernel running, with no synthetic run mutation.
